headline: Australian Property Investor Lending Declines At Record Quarterly Pace
seoTitle: Australian Property Investor Lending Hits Record Low
metaDescription: New data reveals record declines in Australian property investor loans as mortgage delinquency rates among CBA customers reach a 12-year high.
aiSummaryBullets: New lending to property investors in Australia dropped by 31 percent during the third quarter of 2026.
Mortgage repayment difficulties among Commonwealth Bank of Australia customers have increased to a 12-year peak.
Housing Minister Clare O'Neil acknowledged the reduction in investor loan activity amidst shifting market conditions.
aiContextParagraph: The Australian property market is experiencing a significant shift as new lending to investors saw its sharpest recorded decline in the three months leading up to September 2026. Data indicates a 31 percent drop in investor loans during this period, occurring alongside a trend of falling property prices and sustained high interest rates. These market adjustments are compounded by increased tax burdens for landlords, contributing to the departure of investors from the sector. Simultaneously, financial stress among residential borrowers has become more pronounced, with Commonwealth Bank of Australia reporting that customer mortgage delinquency has reached its highest level in 12 years. Housing Minister Clare O'Neil has publicly noted the decline in investor lending activity. This downturn reflects broader economic pressures impacting both individual homeowners and property investors across the country as households struggle to maintain consistent loan repayments within the current fiscal environment.
whyItIsViral: The story is trending due to the record-breaking nature of the lending data and concurrent reports of rising mortgage repayment struggles, captured by two national news outlets.
